package_info.package_versions: All versions prior to 3.0.5.RELEASE (3.x), all versions prior to 2.4.4.RELEASE (1.x, 2.x)
package_info.why_malicious: The package fails to restrict XML External Entity (XXE) processing in its XML parsing utilities, allowing attackers to inject malicious XML that can exfiltrate sensitive data or perform other attacks.

execution_context.file_location: Any code path using DocumentBuilderFactory, XMLInputFactory, or similar XML parsing utilities in spring-ws-core or spring-xml
required_permissions: network (if external entities reference remote resources)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the XML parser processes a crafted XML document containing an external entity reference, causing the application to read the contents of /etc/passwd and potentially return or transmit this data to the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code allows external entity resolution, which can be abused to read arbitrary files or interact with remote resources, leading to data exfiltration or SSRF.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal XML parsing should not allow untrusted input to reference external files or URLs. The actual behavior allows attackers to inject DTDs and access sensitive resources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use of external entities is rare and typically only in trusted, internal XML workflows.
key_indicators: Presence of <!DOCTYPE ... [ <!ENTITY ... SYSTEM ...> ]> in XML input
Use of XML parser factories without secure configuration
Access to sensitive files or remote URLs during XML parsing

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits malicious XML containing an external entity reference.
attack_chain.leads_to: XML parser processes the external entity.

attack_chain.action: XML parser resolves the external entity, reading sensitive file contents (e.g., /etc/passwd).
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is included in the application's XML processing output.

attack_chain.action: Application may return or transmit the sensitive data to the attacker (e.g., in an API response).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive server data.

behavioral_signatures: XML parsing of untrusted input with external entity resolution enabled
Unexpected file or network access during XML parsing
Presence of <!DOCTYPE> and <!ENTITY ... SYSTEM ...> in XML payloads
file_indicators: XML files or payloads containing DOCTYPE and ENTITY definitions
Access to sensitive files (e.g., /etc/passwd, /proc/self/environ) during XML processing
network_indicators: Outbound requests to attacker-controlled domains during XML parsing
Unexpected DNS or HTTP requests triggered by XML entity resolution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor XML parsing code for use of DocumentBuilderFactory, XMLInputFactory, or similar without secure configuration. Inspect logs for XML payloads containing DOCTYPE and ENTITY definitions. Monitor for unexpected file or network access patterns during XML processing, especially when handling user-supplied XML.
